To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the independent variables performance expectation, effort expectation, social influence, facilitating conditions, and experience, as moderated by the experience variable, are statistically related to the intent of a technical project manager to adopt a continuous deployment system.
performance expectancy is significantly related to the behavioral intent to adopt continuous deployment.

The performance expectancy of the DevOps continuous delivery system was the only statistically significant predictor in the model of behavioral intent to use the system, and that the model explained 22% of the variance in behavioral intent to use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to best understand the adoption of continuous delivery by software development project managers.
the adoption of continuous delivery, an advanced software development practice, by technical project managers in large software development organizations.

the relationship between the independent variables of performance expectancy, effort expectation, social influence, facilitating conditions, and experience and the dependent variables of behavioral intent to use continuous delivery.
